eren-jager.name: Eren Yeager
eren-jager.role: Protagonist; member of the Survey Corps

debut.episodeTitle: To You, in 2000 Years: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 1

eren-jager.notes: Arc names follow the Attack on Titan Wiki anime arc pages.
eren-jager.abilities: Discovers during the Battle of Trost that he can transform into a 15-metre Titan, and otherwise fights Titans with blades and vertical maneuvering equipment like the other cadets.

fate.detail: Mikasa kills him by decapitating him in his Titan form during the final battle (manga chapter 138, 2021; adapted in the anime's Final Chapters Special 2, 2023).

l-lawliet.name: L Lawliet
l-lawliet.role: Detective leading the investigation into Kira
l-lawliet.abilities: The world's greatest detective, who works anonymously through deduction, surveillance and psychological traps, often baiting suspects into revealing themselves.

fate.detail: L dies of a heart attack after the Shinigami Rem writes his name in her Death Note to protect Misa (anime episode 25, "Silence"; manga volume 7).

saitama.name: Saitama
saitama.role: Protagonist; hero who can defeat any opponent with one punch
saitama.notes: Chapter number refers to the Yusuke Murata manga; he also debuts in chapter 1 of ONE's webcomic.
saitama.abilities: So overwhelmingly strong that he defeats nearly every opponent with a single punch, a power he says came from a simple daily training routine.

fate.detail: Saitama is alive in both the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026); no death has occurred.

ken-kaneki.name: Ken Kaneki
ken-kaneki.role: Protagonist; university student who becomes a half-ghoul
ken-kaneki.notes: Chapter 1 per the Tokyo Ghoul Wiki; Wikipedia confirms he appears on the volume 1 cover. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
ken-kaneki.abilities: After receiving a ghoul's organs he becomes a half-ghoul with superhuman strength and healing and a rinkaku kagune of tentacles that grows from his back.

fate.detail: Kaneki survives to the end of Tokyo Ghoul:re (2018), marrying Touka and having a daughter; the anime's :re season 2 ends the same way.

mikasa-ackerman.name: Mikasa Ackerman
mikasa-ackerman.role: Eren Yeager's adoptive sister; member of the Survey Corps

debut.episodeTitle: To You, in 2000 Years: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 1

mikasa-ackerman.abilities: The top graduate of the 104th Training Corps, with exceptional speed, strength and skill with vertical maneuvering equipment; she is described as worth a hundred ordinary soldiers.

fate.detail: Mikasa survives the series; the final chapter (139) and the anime's Final Chapters Special 2 show her living on and visiting Eren's grave.

sakura-haruno.name: Sakura Haruno
sakura-haruno.notes: Chapter 3 is confirmed by both sources. The episode 1 anime debut rests on Narutopedia; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 3. Arcs from Kazekage Rescue Mission on are in Naruto: Shippuuden.
sakura-haruno.abilities: A ninja-academy top student with excellent book knowledge and fine chakra control and a sharp eye for spotting genjutsu illusions, though she starts out weaker in combat than her teammates.

fate.detail: Sakura survives the Fourth Shinobi World War and is alive at the end of Naruto (chapter 700), married to Sasuke with a daughter, Sarada.

kakashi-hatake.name: Kakashi Hatake

debut.episodeTitle: Sasuke and Sakura: Friends or Foes?

kakashi-hatake.notes: Chapter 3 is confirmed by both sources. Episode 3 rests on Narutopedia; the Wikipedia summary of episode 3 mentions the team's jonin instructor without naming him. Arcs from Kazekage Rescue Mission on are in Naruto: Shippuuden.
kakashi-hatake.abilities: Known as the Copy Ninja: his Sharingan eye lets him copy other ninjas' techniques, and his signature attack is the lightning-charged Chidori (Lightning Blade).

fate.detail: Kakashi dies of chakra exhaustion fighting Pain during the invasion of Konoha (Shippuden Pain's Assault arc) but is brought back to life when Nagato revives everyone killed in the attack; he survives the series and becomes the Sixth Hokage.

asahi-azumane.name: Asahi Azumane
asahi-azumane.role: Ace wing spiker of Karasuno High's volleyball team
asahi-azumane.notes: Chapter rests on the Haikyuu!! Wiki: briefly seen in chapter 17 ("Storm"), properly introduced in chapter 18. The wiki titles episode 8 "He Who Is Called 'Ace'".
asahi-azumane.abilities: Karasuno's ace wing spiker, the team's physically strongest player, whose powerful spikes can break through blocks.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Haikyu!!; the manga's epilogue shows Asahi working as an apparel designer in Tokyo.

nate-river.name: Nate River
nate-river.role: Successor to L; head of the SPK
nate-river.notes: Episode 26 and chapter 59 ("Zero") rest on the Death Note Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 26 shows two unnamed children and first names Near in episode 27.
nate-river.abilities: A child prodigy detective known as Near, raised at Wammy's House as one of L's potential successors; he solves cases through cold logic while playing with toys and puzzles.

fate.detail: Near survives: he exposes Light as Kira at the Yellow Box warehouse in the final arc and takes over the role of L (manga chapters 103-108; anime episodes 36-37).

touka-kirishima.name: Touka Kirishima
touka-kirishima.role: Ghoul who works as a waitress at the Anteiku café
touka-kirishima.notes: Episode 1 and chapter 1 debut rest on the Tokyo Ghoul Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 3.
touka-kirishima.abilities: A ghoul with an ukaku kagune, a wing-like organ that lets her fight with great speed and fire crystallised shards at range.

fate.detail: Touka survives Tokyo Ghoul:re; by the final chapter she is married to Kaneki and has a daughter, Ichika.

lelouch-lamperouge.name: Lelouch Lamperouge
lelouch-lamperouge.role: Exiled Britannian prince who leads the Black Knights as Zero

debut.anime: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
debut.episodeTitle: The Day a New Demon was Born

lelouch-lamperouge.notes: Code Geass is an original anime, so there is no source chapter.
lelouch-lamperouge.abilities: A brilliant strategist and chess player who gains the Geass of Absolute Obedience, which lets him give any person one command they must obey by making eye contact.

fate.detail: In the final episode of Code Geass R2 (episode 25, 2008), Suzaku, disguised as Zero, stabs Lelouch to death as part of the 'Zero Requiem' plan; the 2019 film Lelouch of the Re;surrection, set in an alternate continuity that follows the compilation films, brings him back to life through C.C.

franky.name: Franky
franky.role: Shipwright of the Straw Hat Pirates

debut.episodeTitle: Pirate Abduction Incident! A Pirate Ship That Can Only Await Her End!

franky.notes: Arcs listed are those covered on the wiki's pre-timeskip history page; he also takes part in every later Straw Hat arc.
franky.abilities: A self-made cyborg shipwright who runs on cola: his rebuilt body hides weapons such as the Strong Right fist and the Fresh Fire breath, and he builds the Straw Hats' ship, the Thousand Sunny.

fate.detail: Franky is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026); he nearly died years earlier, rebuilding his body from scrap after being run over by a sea train.

light-yagami.name: Light Yagami
light-yagami.role: Protagonist; student who uses the Death Note as Kira
light-yagami.abilities: A top-ranked, highly intelligent student who finds the Death Note, a notebook that kills anyone whose name is written in it while the writer pictures the person's face.

fate.detail: After Near exposes him at the Yellow Box warehouse and Matsuda shoots him, Ryuk writes Light's name in his own Death Note and Light dies of a heart attack (manga chapter 107; anime episode 37, where he dies alone on a staircase rather than at the warehouse).

ryuk.name: Ryuk
ryuk.role: Shinigami who drops the Death Note into the human world
ryuk.notes: He also appears in the 2003 one-shot pilot chapter, before the serialized chapter 1.
ryuk.abilities: A Shinigami (death god) who can kill anyone by writing their name in his Death Note, sees people's names and lifespans, flies, and is invisible to anyone who has not touched his notebook.

fate.detail: Ryuk survives; at the end (anime episode 37, manga chapter 107) he writes Light's name in his own Death Note, as he promised at the start, and returns to the Shinigami Realm.

rintarou-okabe.name: Rintarou Okabe
rintarou-okabe.role: Protagonist; self-styled mad scientist who founded the Future Gadget Laboratory
rintarou-okabe.notes: Steins;Gate is adapted from a visual novel (not a manga or light novel), so source is null; the character appears from the start of the game. The wiki gives episode 1 as "Prologue of the Beginning and the End -Turning Point-".
rintarou-okabe.abilities: A self-styled mad scientist whose invention, the PhoneWave, can send text messages to the past; he alone keeps his memories when the timeline changes, an ability he calls Reading Steiner.

fate.detail: Okabe survives the series and reaches the Steins Gate world line in the final episode (24) of the 2011 anime.

meliodas.name: Meliodas
meliodas.role: Captain of the Seven Deadly Sins; owner of the Boar Hat tavern
meliodas.notes: Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
meliodas.abilities: Captain of the Seven Deadly Sins, a swordsman with enormous strength whose signature power, Full Counter, reflects magic attacks back at the attacker with double the force.

fate.detail: Meliodas is killed by Estarossa in the Revival of the Commandments arc, but a curse from the Demon King revives him every time he dies; he survives the series and becomes King of Liones.

kishou-arima.name: Kishou Arima
kishou-arima.role: Special Class Ghoul Investigator of the CCG
kishou-arima.notes: Episode 9 and chapter 29 debut rest on the Tokyo Ghoul Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 9 does not name him. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kishou-arima.abilities: Called the CCG's 'Reaper' and considered undefeated, he is the strongest ghoul investigator, fighting with quinque weapons such as the lightning-firing IXA and Narukami.

fate.detail: After losing to Ken Kaneki in the Cochlea battle, Arima cuts his own throat with his quinque (Tokyo Ghoul:re chapter 82); the 2018 Tokyo Ghoul:re anime adapts his death, while in the earlier Root A anime he survives.

killua-zoldyck.name: Killua Zoldyck
killua-zoldyck.role: Former assassin of the Zoldyck family; Gon's best friend
killua-zoldyck.notes: Chapter 6 is confirmed by both sources. Episode 3 is from the Hunter x Hunter Wiki; the Wikipedia summary introduces him in episode 4 ("Hope × and × Ambition").
killua-zoldyck.abilities: Raised as an assassin by the Zoldyck family, he is extremely fast, resistant to poison and electricity, and can turn his hands into blades.

fate.detail: Killua is alive in the 2011 anime and the manga so far (on hiatus as of November 2026); at the end of the anime he travels with his sister Alluka.

gabi-braun.name: Gabi Braun
gabi-braun.role: Eldian Warrior candidate in Marley; Reiner Braun's cousin

debut.anime: Attack on Titan: The Final Season
debut.episodeTitle: The Other Side of the Sea

gabi-braun.notes: Episode 1 of The Final Season is episode 60 overall. Chapter 91 ("The Other Side of the Ocean") rests on the Attack on Titan Wiki only.
gabi-braun.abilities: A fiercely determined Warrior candidate in Marley's army, and the leading candidate to inherit the Armored Titan; she is athletic, quick-thinking and fearless.

fate.detail: Gabi survives the war and is among the survivors in the final chapter (139) and the anime's Final Chapters Special 2.

osamu-dazai-5df9c678-bb69-4154-84e6-62ec.name: Osamu Dazai
osamu-dazai-5df9c678-bb69-4154-84e6-62ec.role: Member of the Armed Detective Agency; former Port Mafia executive
osamu-dazai-5df9c678-bb69-4154-84e6-62ec.abilities: An Armed Detective Agency member whose ability, No Longer Human, cancels any other supernatural ability he touches; he is also a brilliant strategist.

fate.detail: Dazai is alive in the anime (5 seasons) and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

taiga-aisaka.name: Taiga Aisaka
taiga-aisaka.role: Female lead; Ryuuji Takasu's classmate, nicknamed the Palmtop Tiger
taiga-aisaka.notes: The wiki gives chapter 1 of the first light novel; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover.
taiga-aisaka.abilities: Small but ferocious, she earns the nickname 'Palmtop Tiger' for her violent temper and is not afraid to swing a wooden sword at people.

fate.detail: Taiga is alive at the end of the series (episode 25 of the anime and the final light novel); no character dies in Toradora!.

kurisu-makise.name: Kurisu Makise
kurisu-makise.role: Neuroscience researcher who joins the Future Gadget Laboratory
kurisu-makise.notes: Steins;Gate is adapted from a visual novel (not a manga or light novel), so source is null; the character appears from the start of the game. The wiki gives episode 1 as "Prologue of the Beginning and the End -Turning Point-". Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kurisu-makise.abilities: An 18-year-old neuroscience researcher and genius scientist whose expertise in memory research becomes key to the lab's time-travel experiments.

fate.detail: Kurisu dies in the Beta world line (Okabe accidentally stabs her in episode 23 while trying to save her), but his final time leap rewrites events so she survives in the Steins;Gate world line (episode 24).

kenny-ackerman.name: Kenny Ackerman
kenny-ackerman.role: Leader of the Anti-Personnel Control Squad serving the Reiss family
kenny-ackerman.notes: Season 3 episode 1 is episode 38 overall. Chapter 52 ("Krista Lenz") rests on the Attack on Titan Wiki only. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kenny-ackerman.abilities: A legendary serial killer and Ackerman with superhuman combat instincts who leads the Anti-Personnel Control Squad using guns attached to vertical maneuvering gear.

fate.detail: Fatally burned when Rod Reiss transforms, Kenny dies under a tree after revealing he is Levi's uncle and handing Levi the Titan serum (manga chapter 69; anime Season 3 episode 10, 'Friends').

gowther.name: Gowther
gowther.role: The Goat's Sin of Lust of the Seven Deadly Sins
gowther.notes: Episode 14 is where he is revealed (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a brief cameo in episode 2. Chapter 53 rests on the wiki only.
gowther.abilities: The Seven Deadly Sins' Goat Sin of Lust, who can read and rewrite people's memories and minds with his Invasion power and fires arrows of light from his bow, Herritt.

fate.detail: Gowther survives to the end of the series; it is the original Gowther, the wizard who built him as a doll, who died 3,000 years earlier in the Holy War.

koutaro-bokuto.name: Koutarou Bokuto
koutaro-bokuto.role: Captain and ace of Fukurodani Academy's volleyball team
koutaro-bokuto.notes: Second Season episode 4 is episode 29 overall. Episode and chapter 78 debut rest on the Haikyuu!! Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of that episode does not name him. He appears earlier in the OVA "Lev Genzan!".
koutaro-bokuto.abilities: Fukurodani's captain and ace, a powerful wing spiker ranked among the top five aces in Japan, though his mood swings can suddenly sink his performance.

fate.detail: Bokuto is alive throughout; Haikyu!! is a sports series and the manga ends with him playing professional volleyball for the MSBY Black Jackals.

naruto-uzumaki.name: Naruto Uzumaki
naruto-uzumaki.role: Protagonist; ninja of Konohagakure who aims to become Hokage
naruto-uzumaki.notes: The last two arcs are in Naruto: Shippuuden.
naruto-uzumaki.abilities: A loud, never-give-up ninja who masters the Shadow Clone Jutsu early on and later the Rasengan; the Nine-Tailed Fox sealed inside him gives him vast chakra and stamina.

fate.detail: Naruto survives the series and becomes the Seventh Hokage; in the sequel manga Boruto, Kawaki seals him and Hinata away in a time-frozen dimension with Daikokuten, but he has not died.

sweet-mask.name: Amai Mask
sweet-mask.role: Top-ranked A-Class hero who is also an idol
sweet-mask.notes: Manga chapter left blank: the One Punch Man Wiki lists both chapter 25 and a separate titled chapter as his manga debut.
sweet-mask.abilities: The top-ranked A-Class hero, who refuses promotion to S-Class; he is also a famous idol and is fast and strong enough to destroy monsters with ease.

fate.detail: Amai Mask is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

chikara-ennoshita.name: Chikara Ennoshita
chikara-ennoshita.role: Second-year wing spiker of Karasuno High's volleyball team
chikara-ennoshita.notes: Episode 2 and chapter 10 ("Rookie Nerves") debut rest on the Haikyuu!! Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 2 does not name him.
chikara-ennoshita.abilities: A second-year wing spiker who is a steady, calm substitute rather than a starter, with a level head and quiet leadership.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Haikyu!!; Ennoshita becomes Karasuno's captain after the third-years graduate.

kaoru-hitachiin.name: Kaoru Hitachiin
kaoru-hitachiin.role: Host Club member; one of the Hitachiin twins

debut.episodeTitle: Starting Today, You Are a Host!

kaoru-hitachiin.notes: Episode 1 and chapter 1 debut rest on the Ouran Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 1 refers to the Hosts without naming them.
kaoru-hitachiin.abilities: Performs the Host Club's popular 'forbidden brotherly love' act with his twin Hikaru; the twins are mischievous pranksters who are hard to tell apart.

fate.detail: Kaoru is alive at the end of the series; Ouran High School Host Club is a comedy with no character deaths.

shiro-2.name: Shiro
shiro-2.role: Co-protagonist; half of the undefeated gamer duo Blank
shiro-2.notes: The light novel debut is volume 1; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover.
shiro-2.abilities: A gaming prodigy and half of the undefeated gamer duo Blank; she excels at calculation, chess and other strategy games with machine-like precision.

fate.detail: Shiro is alive in the anime (one season and the Zero film, which follows other characters) and the ongoing light novels.

orihime-inoue.name: Orihime Inoue
orihime-inoue.role: Ichigo Kurosaki's classmate with healing powers
arcs: Arrancar: The Hueco Mundo Sneak Entry
orihime-inoue.notes: Chapter 2 is confirmed by both sources. Episode 2 rests on the Bleach Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 2 does not name her. Arc names are mapped from the Bleach Wiki's manga arcs to the anime arcs in arcs.json.
orihime-inoue.abilities: Her hairpins hold the Shun Shun Rikka, six fairy-like spirits that let her raise barriers, heal injuries by 'rejecting' what happened, and launch a small cutting attack.

fate.detail: Orihime survives the series; the final chapter (686, 2016) shows her married to Ichigo with a son, Kazui.

tenya-iida.name: Tenya Iida
tenya-iida.role: Student in U.A. High School's Class 1-A
tenya-iida.notes: Episode 3 and chapter 3 debut rest on the My Hero Academia Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 3 does not name him.
tenya-iida.abilities: Class 1-A's class representative; his Quirk, Engine, gives him engines in his calves for great running speed.

fate.detail: Iida survives the manga's Final War and is alive at the series ending (chapter 430, 2024).

diego-brando.name: Diego Brando
diego-brando.role: British jockey and rival racer in the Steel Ball Run

debut.anime: Steel Ball Run: JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken

diego-brando.notes: Episode 1 (a 47-minute special that premiered on Netflix on 19 March 2026; episode 191 of the JoJo anime overall) is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 1 of Steel Ball Run rests on the JoJo Wiki only.
diego-brando.abilities: A champion British jockey and one of the race's fastest riders; early in the race he gains the Stand Scary Monsters, which lets him turn himself and others into dinosaurs.

fate.detail: Funny Valentine kills him during the fight on the train near the end of the race; an alternate Diego from a parallel world then takes his place and is destroyed when Lucy Steel forces him to merge with the original Diego's severed head (Steel Ball Run manga).

itaru-hashida.name: Itaru Hashida
itaru-hashida.role: Hacker and Lab Member 003 of the Future Gadget Laboratory
itaru-hashida.notes: Steins;Gate is adapted from a visual novel (not a manga or light novel), so source is null; the character appears from the start of the game. The wiki gives episode 1 as "Prologue of the Beginning and the End -Turning Point-". Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
itaru-hashida.abilities: Lab Member 003, nicknamed Daru: a super-hacker and electronics expert who builds and programs the lab's gadgets.

fate.detail: Daru survives the series in every world line shown; he is the future father of Suzuha.

kurapika.name: Kurapika
kurapika.role: Last survivor of the Kurta Clan, hunting the Phantom Troupe
kurapika.abilities: The last survivor of the Kurta Clan, whose eyes turn scarlet when he is enraged; during the Hunter Exam he fights with twin swords and stands out for his intelligence and calm analysis.

fate.detail: Kurapika is alive in the ongoing manga (Succession War arc, as of November 2026) and at the end of the 2011 anime, although his Emperor Time ability shortens his lifespan each time he uses it.

alois-trancy.name: Alois Trancy
alois-trancy.role: Earl of the Trancy household and master of the butler Claude Faustus
alois-trancy.notes: Created for the Black Butler II anime; the wiki lists no manga debut. Black Butler II episode 1 is episode 25 overall. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
alois-trancy.abilities: The young Earl Trancy, whose real weapon is his contract with the demon butler Claude Faustus, who carries out his orders with inhuman skill.

fate.detail: Claude kills Alois in Black Butler II episode 8, "Divulging Butler"; his soul then lives on inside the demon maid Hannah until the finale (anime-only character).

reiner-braun.name: Reiner Braun
reiner-braun.role: Eren's fellow trainee in the 104th Training Corps

debut.episodeTitle: That Day: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 2

reiner-braun.notes: Episode 2 and chapter 2 debut rest on the Attack on Titan Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name him in episode 3. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
reiner-braun.abilities: One of the top graduates of the 104th Training Corps, admired by the other cadets for his physical strength, reliability and leadership.

fate.detail: Reiner survives the series; he is among the survivors after the final battle, when the power of the Titans disappears (manga chapter 139; anime Final Chapters Special 2, 2023).

olivier-mira-armstrong.name: Olivier Mira Armstrong
olivier-mira-armstrong.role: Major General in command of Fort Briggs
olivier-mira-armstrong.notes: Chapter 63 rests on the Fullmetal Alchemist Wiki only. Arc names follow the wiki's story sections.
olivier-mira-armstrong.abilities: The commander of Fort Briggs, a master swordswoman and tactician with an iron will who runs the northern fortress with strict discipline.

fate.detail: Olivier survives the Promised Day battle and is alive at the end of the series, appearing in the epilogue photo collage.

asuna-yuuki.name: Asuna Yuuki
asuna-yuuki.role: Female lead; sub-leader of the Knights of the Blood guild
asuna-yuuki.notes: Light novel debut is volume 1, chapter 5 (confirmed by both sources). Episode 2 is her first full appearance; the wiki also lists a brief cameo in episode 1.
asuna-yuuki.abilities: One of Aincrad's strongest players, nicknamed 'the Flash' for her lightning-fast rapier attacks, and sub-leader of the Knights of the Blood guild.

fate.detail: Asuna survives: her avatar's HP drops to zero when she shields Kirito from Heathcliff (anime episode 14), but Kirito clears the game and she wakes up in the real world; she is alive in all later arcs.

all-might.name: All Might
all-might.role: Symbol of Peace; top Pro Hero and mentor to Izuku Midoriya
all-might.notes: Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover.
all-might.abilities: The Symbol of Peace and No. 1 Hero, whose Quirk One For All gives him overwhelming strength and speed; an old injury limits how long he can stay in his muscle form.

fate.detail: All Might survives; he retires after the Kamino battle and, despite being badly hurt fighting All For One in the Final War, is alive at the manga's ending (chapter 430) and in the anime's final season.

yuzuru-nishimiya.name: Yuzuru Nishimiya
yuzuru-nishimiya.notes: There is no TV anime: Koe no Katachi (A Silent Voice) is a 2016 film, so episode is null. Chapter 8 rests on the Koe no Katachi Wiki only.
yuzuru-nishimiya.abilities: Shoko's sharp-tongued, fiercely protective younger sister, who goes everywhere with a camera taking photographs.

fate.detail: Yuzuru is alive at the end of both the manga and the 2016 film; no death occurs.

shouhei-fukunaga.name: Shouhei Fukunaga
shouhei-fukunaga.role: Wing spiker of Nekoma High's volleyball team
shouhei-fukunaga.notes: Episode 11 and chapter 27 ("The Cat-Crow Reunion") debut rest on the Haikyuu!! Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 11 does not name him.
shouhei-fukunaga.abilities: Nekoma's quiet second-year wing spiker, known for odd, unpredictable spikes and a quirky sense of humour.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Haikyu!!; Fukunaga is alive through the series ending.

hayase-nagatoro.name: Hayase Nagatoro
hayase-nagatoro.role: Title character; first-year student who teases her senpai

debut.episodeTitle: Senpai is a bit... / Senpai, don't you ever get angry?

hayase-nagatoro.notes: Episode 1 has two segments; both titles are given. Chapter 1 rests on the Nagatoro Wiki only (she also appears in issue 1 of the original webcomic).
hayase-nagatoro.abilities: An athletic, quick-witted first-year whose main talent is relentlessly teasing her shy senpai.

fate.detail: Nagatoro is alive throughout; the series is a romantic comedy with no character deaths.

c-c.name: C.C.
c-c.role: Immortal witch who grants Lelouch the power of Geass

debut.anime: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
debut.episodeTitle: The Day a New Demon was Born

c-c.notes: Code Geass is an original anime, so there is no source chapter.
c-c.abilities: An immortal witch who grants the power of Geass through contracts; she heals from any wound and is immune to ageing.

fate.detail: C.C. is shot dead in the first episode and revives because she is immortal, and she 'dies' repeatedly in the same way; she outlives Lelouch and is alive at the end of R2 (episode 25).

caster-ddbb69e1-54df-4a04-b1c3-767126bbb.name: Caster
caster-ddbb69e1-54df-4a04-b1c3-767126bbb.role: Caster-class Servant of Ryuunosuke Uryuu in the Fourth Holy Grail War
caster-ddbb69e1-54df-4a04-b1c3-767126bbb.notes: His true identity is Gilles de Rais. Episode 2 rests on the Wikipedia episode summary; the TYPE-MOON Wiki confirms him as the Fate/Zero Caster summoned by Ryuunosuke Uryuu but gives no episode. Light novel chapter not confirmed.
caster-ddbb69e1-54df-4a04-b1c3-767126bbb.abilities: A Caster-class Servant (Gilles de Rais) with little magecraft of his own; his grimoire, Prelati's Spellbook, lets him summon near-endless swarms of tentacled sea monsters.

fate.detail: After he summons a giant sea monster on the Mion River, Saber destroys it and him with Excalibur (Fate/Zero, second season, 2012), eliminating him from the Holy Grail War.

ban-b502349e-2c23-449b-82d8-995b8f5f67f6.name: Ban
ban-b502349e-2c23-449b-82d8-995b8f5f67f6.role: The Fox's Sin of Greed of the Seven Deadly Sins
ban-b502349e-2c23-449b-82d8-995b8f5f67f6.notes: Chapter 7 rests on the Seven Deadly Sins Wiki only.
ban-b502349e-2c23-449b-82d8-995b8f5f67f6.abilities: The Fox Sin of Greed, made immortal by drinking from the Fountain of Youth; his power Snatch lets him steal physical strength and objects from opponents.

fate.detail: Ban survives the series; he later gives up his immortality to bring Elaine back to life, marries her and rules the Kingdom of Benwick.

tobio-kageyama.name: Tobio Kageyama
tobio-kageyama.role: Setter for Karasuno High's volleyball team
tobio-kageyama.notes: Wikipedia notes his sister Miwa appears only in the manga.
tobio-kageyama.abilities: A genius setter once called the 'King of the Court', with pinpoint-accurate tosses, a powerful serve and lightning-quick reactions.

fate.detail: Kageyama is alive at the end of the manga (chapter 402, 2020), playing professional volleyball; Haikyu!! has no character deaths.

suguha-kirigaya.name: Suguha Kirigaya
suguha-kirigaya.role: Kirito's younger sister; plays ALfheim Online as Leafa

relatives.name: Kazuto Kirigaya
relatives.relation: cousin, raised as her older brother

suguha-kirigaya.notes: Episode 15 is her first full appearance (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a brief cameo in episode 1. Light novel volume 3 (prologue) rests on the wiki only.
suguha-kirigaya.abilities: A national-level kendo competitor; in the game ALfheim Online she plays Leafa, a fast Sylph swordswoman and flier.

fate.detail: Suguha is alive through every adapted arc and the ongoing light novels.

armin-arelet.name: Armin Arlert
armin-arelet.role: Childhood friend of Eren and Mikasa; member of the Survey Corps

debut.episodeTitle: To You, in 2000 Years: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 1

armin-arelet.notes: Episode 1 and chapter 1 debut rest on the Attack on Titan Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name him in episode 2.
armin-arelet.abilities: Physically the weakest of his friends, but a brilliant strategist whose quick thinking repeatedly finds a way out against the Titans.

fate.detail: Armin survives the series; he is badly burned and close to death in the Battle of Shiganshina (manga chapter 84) but is saved with the Titan serum, and in the final chapter (139) he leads the Allied peace delegation.

karma-akabane.name: Karma Akabane
karma-akabane.role: Student of Class 3-E at Kunugigaoka Junior High School
karma-akabane.notes: Episode 3 is his proper introduction (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a cameo in episode 2. Chapter 3 rests on the wiki only.
karma-akabane.abilities: The cleverest troublemaker in Class 3-E, a skilled street fighter and cunning strategist who is one of the class's best assassins.

fate.detail: Karma survives the series; in the seven-years-later epilogue he has passed the exams to become a government official.

alphonse-elric.name: Alphonse Elric
alphonse-elric.role: Co-protagonist; Edward Elric's younger brother, whose soul is bound to a suit of armor
alphonse-elric.abilities: A gifted alchemist whose soul is bound to a giant suit of armour; the armour makes him a powerful hand-to-hand fighter who never tires, eats or sleeps.

fate.detail: Al survives: in the final battle he trades his soul to restore Edward's arm, and Edward then gives up his own alchemy to bring Al back with his original body (manga chapter 108; Brotherhood episode 63).

ami-kawashima.name: Ami Kawashima
ami-kawashima.role: Teen fashion model and Yusaku Kitamura's childhood friend who transfers into Ryuuji's class
ami-kawashima.notes: Episode 5 is confirmed by both sources. Light novel volume 2 rests on the Toradora! Wiki only.
ami-kawashima.abilities: A popular teen fashion model who hides a sharp, manipulative personality behind a sweet 'perfect girl' act, and is very perceptive about other people's feelings.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Toradora!; Ami is alive at the end of the anime and light novels.

argo.name: Argo
argo.role: Information broker in Sword Art Online, nicknamed "Argo the Rat"
argo.notes: Episode 3 rests on the Sword Art Online Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 3 does not name her. Light novel volume left blank: the wiki says she is first mentioned in volume 2 and first appears in person in Progressive volume 1.
argo.abilities: An information broker nicknamed 'the Rat' who sells intel about Aincrad; she is quick, stealthy and hard to catch.

fate.detail: Argo survives Sword Art Online and is logged out when Kirito clears the game.

asia-argento.name: Asia Argento
asia-argento.role: Former nun with the healing Sacred Gear Twilight Healing; member of the Occult Research Club
asia-argento.notes: Episode 2 (she is bumped into at the end) and light novel volume 1 rest on the High School DxD Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 3.
asia-argento.abilities: A gentle former nun whose Sacred Gear, Twilight Healing, can heal any wound, including those of devils.

fate.detail: Asia dies when Raynare rips out her Sacred Gear (light novel volume 1, adapted in the first anime season), and Rias revives her as a Devil and her Bishop; she is alive afterwards.

atomic-samurai.name: Atomic Samurai
atomic-samurai.role: S-Class swordsman hero of the Hero Association
atomic-samurai.notes: His real name is Kamikaze. Chapter number refers to the Yusuke Murata manga.
atomic-samurai.abilities: An S-Class hero and master swordsman whose signature Atomic Slash cuts an enemy into countless pieces in an instant.

fate.detail: Atomic Samurai is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

barry-the-chopper.name: Barry the Chopper
barry-the-chopper.role: Serial killer whose soul is bound to a suit of armor guarding the Fifth Laboratory
barry-the-chopper.notes: Episode 7 (where he attacks Alphonse as "66") and chapter 11 rest on the Fullmetal Alchemist Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name him in episode 8.
barry-the-chopper.abilities: A serial killer's soul bound to a suit of armour, fighting with meat cleavers; as an armour body he feels no pain and cannot tire.

fate.detail: In Brotherhood and the manga, Lust slashes his armour apart beneath Laboratory 3 and his dying original body then scratches out his blood seal, killing body and soul together; in the 2003 anime he survives longer.

bertolt-hoover.name: Bertolt Hoover
bertolt-hoover.role: Reserved member of the 104th Training Corps and Reiner Braun's close friend

debut.episodeTitle: That Day: The Fall of Shiganshina, Part 2

bertolt-hoover.notes: Episode 2 (a brief appearance) rests on the Attack on Titan Wiki episode page; Wikipedia episode summaries first name him in episode 3. Manga chapter left blank because the listed debut chapter would spoil a plot reveal. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
bertolt-hoover.abilities: A quiet, highly ranked cadet of the 104th Training Corps with strong all-round skills, though he lacks initiative and tends to follow Reiner.

fate.detail: Armin, turned into a mindless Titan, eats him to inherit the Colossal Titan during the Battle of Shiganshina (manga chapter 84; anime season 3 episode 18, 'Midnight Sun').

bishamon.name: Bishamon
bishamon.role: Goddess of war and fortune who holds a grudge against Yato
bishamon.notes: Episode 5 and chapter 6 rest on the Noragami Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 5 does not name her. She is also called Bishamonten and Veena.
bishamon.abilities: One of the Seven Lucky Gods, a powerful war goddess who fights with a large retinue of regalia, including guns, a whip and a lion.

fate.detail: Bishamon is alive at the end of the manga (concluded 2023) and in the anime.

caynz.name: Caynz
caynz.role: Former member of the Golden Apple guild and Yolko's boyfriend
caynz.notes: Episode 5 is confirmed by both sources. Light novel volume 8 ("A Murder Case in the Area") rests on the Sword Art Online Wiki only.

fate.detail: His apparent murder inside a safe zone (anime episode 5, 'Murder in the Safe Zone') is staged with Yolko to catch a killer; he survives and is logged out when Kirito clears the game.

chainsaw-man-aki-hayakawa.name: Aki Hayakawa
chainsaw-man-aki-hayakawa.role: Public Safety Devil Hunter in Tokyo Special Division 4 and Denji's senior partner
chainsaw-man-aki-hayakawa.notes: Episode 2 is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 3 rests on the Chainsaw Man Wiki only.
chainsaw-man-aki-hayakawa.abilities: A Public Safety devil hunter who fights with a katana and contracts with devils, chiefly the Fox Devil, which he summons to bite enemies.

fate.detail: In the Gun Devil arc of the manga's Part 1 the Gun Devil takes over his body, turning him into the Gun Fiend, and Denji kills him; this has not been animated yet as of November 2026.

charlotte-265064b8-abef-46a5-a01f-fc929b.name: Charlotte
charlotte-265064b8-abef-46a5-a01f-fc929b.role: Princess of Albion, fourth in line to the throne, who works with a team of spies at Queen's Mayfair School
charlotte-265064b8-abef-46a5-a01f-fc929b.notes: Usually called "Princess". Princess Principal is an original anime, so there is no source chapter. Episodes air out of story order; episode 1 is "Case 13". Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
charlotte-265064b8-abef-46a5-a01f-fc929b.abilities: A princess of Albion, fourth in line to the throne, who works alongside a team of spies; her strengths are political skill, composure and resolve rather than combat.

fate.detail: Charlotte is alive at the end of the TV series and in the Crown Handler film chapters released so far.

chihiro-ogino.name: Chihiro Ogino
chihiro-ogino.role: Protagonist; ten-year-old girl who works in Yubaba's bathhouse to free her parents
chihiro-ogino.notes: Spirited Away is a 2001 film with an original story, so episode and source are null. She is called Sen for most of the film.
chihiro-ogino.abilities: An ordinary 10-year-old girl with no powers who shows courage, hard work and loyalty while working in the spirits' bathhouse.

fate.detail: Chihiro survives and returns to the human world with her parents at the end of the film.

claude-faustus.name: Claude Faustus
claude-faustus.role: Demon butler of the Trancy household, bound by contract to Alois Trancy
claude-faustus.notes: Created for the Black Butler II anime; the wiki lists no manga debut. Black Butler II episode 1 is episode 25 overall. Arc name follows Alois Trancy's entry.
claude-faustus.abilities: A demon butler bound to Alois Trancy, flawless at household duties and a fighter on Sebastian's level who uses golden cutlery as weapons and spider-like threads.

fate.detail: In the Black Butler II finale (episode 12), Sebastian stabs him with the demon sword Laevatein during their duel, and he dies beside Hannah.

emilia-3.name: Emilia
emilia-3.role: Main heroine; half-elf candidate in the royal selection for the throne of Lugunica

debut.episodeTitle: The End of the Beginning and the Beginning of the End

emilia-3.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources. Light novel volume 1 rests on the Re:Zero Wiki; Wikipedia gives her web novel debut in the prologue. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
emilia-3.abilities: A half-elf spirit arts user who fights with ice magic, aided by her contracted great spirit, the cat Puck.

fate.detail: Emilia is alive in the anime (through season 3) and the ongoing light novels; she is killed in some of the timelines that Subaru erases with Return by Death, but those deaths are undone.

erina-nakiri.name: Erina Nakiri
erina-nakiri.role: Granddaughter of Totsuki Culinary Academy's dean, known for her "God Tongue"
erina-nakiri.notes: Episode 2 is her full introduction (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a cameo in episode 1 and chapter 1. Chapter 2 and the Elite Ten seat rest on the Food Wars! Wiki only. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
erina-nakiri.abilities: She has the 'God Tongue', a palate so refined it detects every flaw in a dish, and is a prodigy chef and member of Totsuki's Elite Ten.

fate.detail: Erina is alive at the end of the manga and anime (Food Wars! The Fifth Plate, 2020).

finnian.name: Finnian
finnian.role: Gardener of the Phantomhive household with superhuman strength
finnian.notes: Usually called Finny. Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he appears in the first manga volume.
finnian.abilities: The Phantomhive gardener, a clumsy-seeming boy with monstrous superhuman strength, the result of experiments done on him, who helps defend the manor.

fate.detail: Finnian is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

finral-roulacase.name: Finral Roulacase
finral-roulacase.role: Black Bulls Magic Knight who uses Spatial Magic for transport
arcs: Eye of the Midnight Sun Encounter
finral-roulacase.notes: Episode 4 and chapter 2 rest on the Black Clover Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 4 does not name him. Arcs follow mentions in his wiki biography.
finral-roulacase.abilities: A Black Bulls spatial mage whose Spatial Magic opens portals for instant travel, making him the squad's transport and escape route.

fate.detail: Finral is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

genos.name: Genos
genos.role: Cyborg hero who becomes Saitama's disciple
genos.notes: Episode 2 is his first full appearance (confirmed by both sources); the wiki also lists a brief appearance at the end of episode 1. Chapter 5 of the Murata manga rests on the One Punch Man Wiki only.
genos.abilities: A teenage cyborg and Saitama's self-declared disciple who fights with incineration cannons in his arms and constantly upgraded parts.

fate.detail: Genos is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026); his body is wrecked in many fights, but Dr. Kuseno rebuilds him each time.

gon-freecss.name: Gon Freecss
gon-freecss.role: Protagonist; boy who sets out to become a Hunter and find his father
gon-freecss.abilities: A boy raised on Whale Island with keen animal-like senses, huge stamina and agility; at the start he fights with a fishing rod.

fate.detail: Gon survives: his forced transformation against Neferpitou in the Chimera Ant arc leaves him near death, Alluka heals him in the Election arc, and he loses access to Nen.

gray-fullbuster.name: Gray Fullbuster
gray-fullbuster.role: Ice-Make wizard of the Fairy Tail guild and member of Team Natsu
gray-fullbuster.notes: Episode 2 and chapter 2 rest on the Fairy Tail Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 2 does not name him. Debut is in the 2009 series. Arc names follow the wiki synopsis. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
gray-fullbuster.abilities: A Fairy Tail wizard who uses Ice-Make magic to shape ice into weapons and shields, and has a habit of stripping off his clothes without noticing.

fate.detail: Gray is killed shielding Juvia during the dragon attack at the end of the Grand Magic Games arc, but Ultear's time-reversal spell, Last Ages, undoes his death; he is alive at the end of Fairy Tail.

haku-e244892b-b626-4c5f-a509-b7c600052bf.name: Haku
haku-e244892b-b626-4c5f-a509-b7c600052bf.role: Boy at the witch Yubaba's bathhouse who helps Chihiro after she enters the spirit world
haku-e244892b-b626-4c5f-a509-b7c600052bf.notes: Spirited Away is a film, so episode is null; it is an original Studio Ghibli story with no manga or light novel source. His true identity is left out to avoid spoilers.
haku-e244892b-b626-4c5f-a509-b7c600052bf.abilities: Yubaba's apprentice, a boy who uses magic and can transform into a white dragon.

fate.detail: Haku is alive at the end of the film after Chihiro helps him remember his true name.

heen.name: Heen
heen.notes: Howl's Moving Castle is a film, so episode is null; it adapts Diana Wynne Jones's prose novel, so source is null. The Ghibli Wiki notes he was created for the film and does not appear in the novel.
heen.abilities: Madame Suliman's wheezing old dog, sent as a spy, who later loyally helps Sophie and her companions.

fate.detail: Heen survives the film and stays with Sophie's household at the end.

hero-6e47f7e6-abaf-453a-9b48-41ec706bdb9.name: Ren Amamiya
hero-6e47f7e6-abaf-453a-9b48-41ec706bdb9.role: Protagonist; transfer student at Shujin Academy who leads the Phantom Thieves of Hearts as Joker

debut.episodeTitle: I Am Thou, Thou Art I

hero-6e47f7e6-abaf-453a-9b48-41ec706bdb9.notes: He is the protagonist of the video game Persona 5, so source is null; the name Ren Amamiya is the one used in the anime. Episode 1 rests on the Wikipedia episode summary. A separate TV special, The Day Breakers, aired in 2016 before the series.
hero-6e47f7e6-abaf-453a-9b48-41ec706bdb9.abilities: A transfer student who awakens the Persona Arsène and leads the Phantom Thieves of Hearts; unlike his friends, he can switch between multiple Personas.

fate.detail: Ren survives the series; Akechi's attempt to kill him in the interrogation room is foiled by the Phantom Thieves' plan, so his death is only faked.

hinami-fueguchi.name: Hinami Fueguchi
hinami-fueguchi.role: Young ghoul who comes to the 20th Ward with her mother and grows close to Ken Kaneki at Anteiku
hinami-fueguchi.notes: Episode 3 and chapter 10 debut rest on the Tokyo Ghoul Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 3 does not name her. Wikipedia mentions her mother and father; their names rest on the wiki. Arc names follow the wiki's plot sections; the last four are in Tokyo Ghoul:re.
hinami-fueguchi.abilities: A young ghoul with an exceptionally keen sense of smell, even for a ghoul; she starts out sheltered and unwilling to fight.

fate.detail: Hinami survives to the end of Tokyo Ghoul:re.

hisashi-igou.name: Hisashi Igou
hisashi-igou.role: Fujimi High School student; Takashi Komuro's best friend and Rei Miyamoto's boyfriend
hisashi-igou.notes: Wikipedia spells his surname Igo. Episode 1 rests on the Wikipedia episode summary; the wiki gives no episode. Manga chapter not confirmed.
hisashi-igou.abilities: An athletic Fujimi High student, loyal to his best friend Takashi and his girlfriend Rei.

fate.detail: Bitten by one of 'them' in the first episode ('Spring of the DEAD'), he dies of the infection before Takashi can kill him and turns into one of the undead.

hiyori-iki.name: Hiyori Iki
hiyori-iki.role: Middle school girl who becomes a half-phantom after saving Yato from a bus accident

debut.episodeTitle: A Housecat, a Stray God, and a Tail

hiyori-iki.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 2 rests on the Noragami Wiki only. Relatives are listed only on the wiki, so they are left out.
hiyori-iki.abilities: After an accident she becomes a half-phantom whose soul can leave her body, letting her move with great agility and see gods and phantoms; she also practises kick-heavy fighting.

fate.detail: Hiyori is alive at the end of the Noragami manga (concluded 2023) and in the anime.

howl.name: Howl
howl.role: Wizard whose moving castle Sophie enters; he dodges the king's summons to fight in the war
howl.notes: Howl's Moving Castle is a film, so episode is null; it adapts Diana Wynne Jones's prose novel, so source is null. Wikipedia notes he uses the aliases Jenkins and Pendragon.
howl.abilities: A powerful, vain wizard who lives in a walking castle, goes by several aliases, and can transform into a bird-like creature.

fate.detail: Howl survives the film; Sophie returns his heart and he lives on with her.

izuku-midoriya.name: Izuku Midoriya
izuku-midoriya.role: Protagonist; U.A. High School student training to become a Pro Hero
izuku-midoriya.abilities: A born-Quirkless boy who inherits All Might's One For All, a power so strong it breaks his own bones at first; he is also an analytical hero nerd who studies other Quirks.

fate.detail: Deku survives the Final War and the series; the manga's ending (chapter 430) shows him losing One For All, teaching at U.A., and eight years later returning to hero work in a powered suit.

jibril.name: Jibril
jibril.role: Flügel who lives in Elkia's library and serves Sora and Shiro after losing a game to them
jibril.notes: Light novel debut is volume 2 (the wiki, and Wikipedia cites volume 2 for her introduction). Episode 5 is her first full appearance; the wiki also lists a cameo in episode 1.
jibril.abilities: A Flügel, one of a warlike angelic race; she has immense magical power, can teleport, and is obsessed with collecting knowledge and books.

fate.detail: Jibril is alive in the anime and the ongoing light novels.

jonathan-joestar.name: Jonathan Joestar
jonathan-joestar.role: Protagonist of Part 1, Phantom Blood; son of the Joestar family who becomes rivals with his adoptive brother Dio Brando
jonathan-joestar.notes: Descendants are left out to avoid spoilers.
jonathan-joestar.abilities: A strong, gentlemanly rugby player who learns Hamon (the Ripple), a breathing technique that channels sunlight energy to destroy vampires and zombies.

fate.detail: At the end of Part 1, Phantom Blood (1889; anime episode 9), Jonathan dies of a wound from Dio's severed head on his honeymoon ship, using his last Ripple to save Erina.

jujutsu-kaisen-nobara-kugisaki.name: Nobara Kugisaki
jujutsu-kaisen-nobara-kugisaki.role: First-year student at Tokyo Jujutsu High alongside Yuji Itadori and Megumi Fushiguro
jujutsu-kaisen-nobara-kugisaki.notes: Chapter 3 is confirmed by both sources (the wiki also notes she is on the chapter 1 cover). Episode 2 rests on the Jujutsu Kaisen Wiki; the Wikipedia summaries first name her in episode 3.
jujutsu-kaisen-nobara-kugisaki.abilities: A first-year sorcerer who uses the Straw Doll Technique, hammering cursed nails with her hammer and using Resonance to strike enemies through a straw doll.

fate.detail: Mahito's Idle Transfiguration hits her face in the Shibuya Incident (manga chapter 125; anime season 2), leaving her fate unknown for years; she returns alive, missing her left eye, in chapter 253 (2024) and is alive at the series' end (chapter 271).

jujutsu-kaisen-yuji-itadori.name: Yuji Itadori
jujutsu-kaisen-yuji-itadori.role: Protagonist; high schooler who becomes the vessel of Ryomen Sukuna and joins Tokyo Jujutsu High
jujutsu-kaisen-yuji-itadori.notes: Other relatives are left out to avoid spoilers.
jujutsu-kaisen-yuji-itadori.abilities: A boy with superhuman physical strength and speed who becomes the vessel of the curse Sukuna after eating one of his fingers, and fights with powerful cursed-energy punches.

fate.detail: Yuji dies in the Cursed Womb arc (anime episode 5) when Sukuna tears out his heart, but Sukuna revives him; he survives to the manga's ending (chapter 271, 2024).

juliet-persia.name: Juliet Persia
juliet-persia.role: Female lead; first-year leader of the White Cat Dormitory at Dahlia Academy
juliet-persia.notes: Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
juliet-persia.abilities: Leader of the White Cats first-years (West Rhombus) at Dahlia Academy, a skilled swordswoman and fighter who wants to end the rivalry between the two dorms.

fate.detail: Juliet is alive at the end of the manga; the series is a romantic comedy with no character deaths.

justin.name: Turnip Head
justin.role: Enchanted living scarecrow who leads Sophie to Howl's castle
justin.notes: Howl's Moving Castle is a film, so episode is null; it adapts Diana Wynne Jones's prose novel, so source is null. His true identity is left out to avoid spoilers.
justin.abilities: A silent, hopping scarecrow with a turnip head who is cursed; despite having no voice, he guides and helps Sophie on her journey.

fate.detail: He survives; Sophie's kiss breaks his curse at the end of the film, revealing him as Prince Justin of the neighbouring kingdom.

kaede-kayano.name: Kaede Kayano
kaede-kayano.role: Student of Class 3-E at Kunugigaoka Junior High School and close friend of Nagisa Shiota
kaede-kayano.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 1 rests on the wiki only. She also appears in the earlier Jump Festa event anime (both sources list its voice actress). Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kaede-kayano.abilities: A cheerful Class 3-E student who loves sweets and gives Koro-sensei his name; she starts out looking like an ordinary member of the class.

fate.detail: In the final battle she is impaled through the chest by the second Reaper while protecting Koro-sensei; he preserves her blood and cells, rebuilds the damage and restarts her heart, bringing her back to life (anime season 2), and she survives the series.

kaori-miyazono.name: Kaori Miyazono
kaori-miyazono.role: Violinist who pushes Kousei Arima to return to performing
kaori-miyazono.notes: Chapter 1 ("Monotone") per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover. Relatives are listed only on the wiki, so they are left out.
kaori-miyazono.abilities: A free-spirited violinist who ignores the score to play with bold, emotional expression that wins audiences over.

fate.detail: Kaori dies during a risky operation for her illness while Kousei plays in the Eastern Japan Piano Competition finals (final episode 22; end of the manga).

katsuki-bakugou.name: Katsuki Bakugou
katsuki-bakugou.role: Izuku Midoriya's childhood friend and rival; student in U.A. High School's Class 1-A
katsuki-bakugou.notes: Chapter 1 is confirmed by both sources. Episode 1 rests on the My Hero Academia Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 1 does not name him.
katsuki-bakugou.abilities: His Quirk, Explosion, ignites the nitroglycerin-like sweat from his palms, giving him blasts for attacks and mobility; he is also a combat prodigy with sharp instincts.

fate.detail: In the final war Shigaraki bursts his heart and he dies briefly, but Edgeshot repairs his heart and he is revived (manga, 2022; anime season 7, 2024); he survives the series.

kazu-ishi.name: Kazu Ishii
kazu-ishi.role: Fujimi student who stays with the school nurse Shizuka Marikawa and tries to protect her when the outbreak starts
kazu-ishi.notes: Both sources spell his surname Ishii (AniLumi lists him as Kazu Ishi). Debut episode and chapter not confirmed: neither source gives them, and the English Wikipedia episode summaries do not name him. Role confirmed by the Highschool of the Dead Wiki and the Japanese Wikipedia character list.

fate.detail: In the first episode (and the manga's opening), Kazu is bitten while fleeing the school, and Saeko Busujima kills him at his request before he can turn into one of Them.

kenma-kozume.name: Kenma Kozume
kenma-kozume.role: Setter for Nekoma High's volleyball team
kenma-kozume.notes: Episode 11 is confirmed by both sources (the wiki titles it "Decision"). Chapter 24 ("Go, Team Karasuno!") rests on the Haikyuu!! Wiki only.
kenma-kozume.abilities: Nekoma's setter and the team's 'brain': calm, observant and quick to read opponents' habits and weaknesses, though not physically strong.

fate.detail: Kenma is alive at the end of the manga (chapter 402, 2020), running his own business and gaming career; Haikyu!! has no character deaths.

kirei-kotomine.name: Kirei Kotomine
kirei-kotomine.role: Priest chosen as a Master in the Fourth Holy Grail War
kirei-kotomine.notes: Episode 1 rests on the Wikipedia episode summary; the TYPE-MOON Wiki confirms his Fate/Zero role but gives no episode. Light novel chapter not confirmed. He first appeared in the Fate/stay night visual novel (2004), where he oversees the Fifth Holy Grail War. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
kirei-kotomine.abilities: A former Church executor who fights with Black Keys (thrown blade-hilts) and Bajiquan martial arts, and is a skilled healer; he is a Master in the Fourth Holy Grail War.

fate.detail: Kiritsugu shoots him through the heart in their final duel (Fate/Zero episode 24), but the corrupted Grail revives him (episode 25); he then dies for good in all three routes of the sequel, Fate/stay night.

koma-enji.name: Enji Koma
koma-enji.role: Ghoul waiter at the Anteiku café
koma-enji.notes: Episode 3 and chapter 14 debut rest on the Tokyo Ghoul Wiki; the Wikipedia episode summaries do not name him.
koma-enji.abilities: A playful Anteiku waiter who, as a ghoul, is a strong hand-to-hand fighter able to hold his own against top CCG investigators.

fate.detail: Koma survives the Owl Suppression Operation and reappears alive in Tokyo Ghoul:re as a member of Goat (manga), but the anime cuts him from :re; the series wiki lists him as deceased without describing a death.

konata-izumi.name: Konata Izumi
konata-izumi.role: Protagonist; otaku high school girl at the centre of the Lucky Star friend group
konata-izumi.notes: Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover. The manga is a four-panel strip, so no chapter number is given.
konata-izumi.abilities: An otaku with a gift for games and anime trivia who is also surprisingly athletic and skilled at martial arts, though she avoids clubs to play games.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Lucky Star; Konata is alive throughout the anime and manga.

koneko-toujou.name: Koneko Toujou
koneko-toujou.role: Rook of Rias Gremory's peerage; Kuoh Academy student in the Occult Research Club
koneko-toujou.notes: Episode 1 rests on the High School DxD Wiki episode page; the Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 2. Light novel volume not confirmed.
koneko-toujou.abilities: A member of Rias Gremory's peerage with the Rook's monstrous strength and defence, fighting with her bare fists.

fate.detail: Koneko is alive in the anime (High School DxD Hero, 2018) and the light novels.

kousei-arima.name: Kousei Arima
kousei-arima.role: Protagonist; former child piano prodigy who stopped playing after his mother died
kousei-arima.notes: Chapter 1 ("Monotone") per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover.
kousei-arima.abilities: A former child prodigy pianist, nicknamed the 'human metronome' for his precise playing, who can no longer hear his own piano after his mother's death.

fate.detail: Kousei survives the series and keeps playing the piano.

krul-tepes.name: Krul Tepes
krul-tepes.role: Third Progenitor and vampire queen of Japan
krul-tepes.notes: Role is confirmed by both sources. Episode 1 and chapter 1 of the main Vampire Reign manga rest on the Seraph of the End Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 1 does not name her. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
krul-tepes.abilities: The vampire queen of Japan and a Third Progenitor, vastly stronger and faster than ordinary vampires.

fate.detail: The anime (2015) ends with her alive, but in the ongoing manga (chapter 138) she is devoured by Ferid Bathory after drinking Guren's blood and survives only as a consciousness trapped inside Ferid, where she vanishes in chapter 150.

leorio-paladiknight.name: Leorio Paradinight
leorio-paladiknight.role: Hunter Exam applicant who wants to become a doctor; friend of Gon, Killua and Kurapika
leorio-paladiknight.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources; chapter 2 rests on the Hunter x Hunter Wiki only. Arcs follow the wiki's plot sections.
leorio-paladiknight.abilities: A Hunter Exam candidate who wants to become a doctor; he is tough, loyal and quick-tempered, and fights with a knife and briefcase.

fate.detail: Leorio is alive in the 2011 anime and the manga so far (on hiatus as of November 2026).

levi.name: Levi Ackerman
levi.role: Survey Corps captain who leads the Special Operations Squad; called humanity's strongest soldier

debut.episodeTitle: The Night of the Closing Ceremony: Humanity's Comeback, Part 2

levi.notes: Episode 4 debut rests on the Attack on Titan Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name him in episode 9. His manga debut is the 2010 side story "Captain Levi" rather than a numbered chapter (both sources), so chapter is null. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
levi.abilities: Known as humanity's strongest soldier: captain of the Survey Corps' Special Operations Squad, unmatched with vertical maneuvering equipment and blades.

fate.detail: Levi survives the series, though he loses two fingers and an eye; the final chapter (139) and Final Chapters Special 2 show him in a wheelchair after the war.

lord-yupa.name: Lord Yupa
lord-yupa.role: Wandering swordsmaster of the Valley of the Wind and Nausicaä's teacher

debut.anime: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind

lord-yupa.notes: Nausicaä of the Valley of the Wind is a 1984 film, not a TV series, so episode is null. He also appears in Hayao Miyazaki's manga; chapter not confirmed.
lord-yupa.abilities: Known as the greatest swordsman in the Periphery, a wandering warrior and scholar who investigates the Sea of Corruption.

fate.detail: Yupa survives the 1984 film; in Miyazaki's manga, however, he dies sacrificing himself to protect Kushana from an attack.

lucy-steel.name: Lucy Steel
lucy-steel.role: Fourteen-year-old wife of Steel Ball Run organizer Steven Steel

debut.anime: Steel Ball Run: JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken

lucy-steel.notes: Wikipedia lists her in the anime cast, but neither source gives an anime debut episode, so episode is null. Chapter 1 of Steel Ball Run rests on the JoJo Wiki only.
lucy-steel.abilities: The 14-year-old wife of race promoter Steven Steel; with no Stand or fighting skills at first, she relies on nerve and quick thinking.

fate.detail: Lucy survives the story; after the race she defeats the alternate Diego and returns safely to Steven (Steel Ball Run manga).

mami-tomoe.name: Mami Tomoe
mami-tomoe.role: Veteran magical girl and third-year student who mentors Madoka and Sayaka

debut.episodeTitle: I First Met Her in a Dream... or Something.

mami-tomoe.notes: Episode title as in the Wikipedia episode list; her Wikipedia article renders it "As If I Met Her in My Dream...". Madoka Magica is an original anime (the manga adapts it), so there is no source chapter. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
mami-tomoe.abilities: A veteran magical girl who fights with summoned muskets and her signature finishing attack, Tiro Finale.

fate.detail: The witch Charlotte bites off her head in episode 3; after Madoka's wish remakes the universe in episode 12 she exists again in the new world, and she returns in the Rebellion film.

markl.name: Markl
markl.notes: Howl's Moving Castle is a 2004 film, so episode is null. The film is based on Diana Wynne Jones's novel (not a manga or light novel), so source is null.
markl.abilities: Howl's young apprentice, who looks after the castle's door and uses a cloak spell to look like an old man when dealing with customers.

fate.detail: Markl is alive at the end of the film.

mayoi-hachikuji.name: Mayoi Hachikuji
mayoi-hachikuji.role: Elementary school girl Koyomi Araragi meets while she is lost
mayoi-hachikuji.notes: Wikipedia titles episode 3 "Mayoi Mai Mai, Part One". Her story is part of the Bakemonogatari light novel; volume and chapter not confirmed. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
mayoi-hachikuji.abilities: A ghost girl, the snail apparition that makes people lost on their way, and a quick-witted talker known for mangling Araragi's name.

fate.detail: Mayoi is already dead when introduced, the ghost of a girl killed in a traffic accident 11 years earlier; she passes on in Onimonogatari, then meets Araragi in hell (Owarimonogatari, Mayoi Hell) and returns to become the goddess of the North Shirahebi Shrine.

mayuri-shiina.name: Mayuri Shiina
mayuri-shiina.role: Rintarou Okabe's childhood friend and Lab Member 002 of the Future Gadget Laboratory
mayuri-shiina.notes: Steins;Gate is adapted from a visual novel (not a manga or light novel), so source is null. The wiki gives episode 1 as "Prologue of the Beginning and the End -Turning Point-". Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
mayuri-shiina.abilities: Okabe's cheerful childhood friend and lab member, a skilled cosplay costume maker who works part-time at a maid cafe.

fate.detail: She dies again and again in the Alpha worldline from episode 12 onward no matter what Okabe changes, but he finally reaches the Steins;Gate worldline where she survives (episode 24).

mikuru-asahina.name: Mikuru Asahina
mikuru-asahina.role: Time traveler from the future who is pulled into the SOS Brigade

debut.episodeTitle: The Adventures of Mikuru Asahina Episode 00

mikuru-asahina.notes: Episode 1 follows the 2006 broadcast order, which opens with the SOS Brigade's film; the Wikipedia summary of the first episode in chronological order also names her. Light novel debut is the first novel, The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya (both sources).
mikuru-asahina.abilities: A timid time traveller from the future who can travel back through time (with Kyon in tow), though she is forbidden to reveal most details about it.

fate.detail: Mikuru is alive throughout the anime and the light novels (the series has had no new volume since 2020).

milly-ashford.name: Milly Ashford
milly-ashford.role: Student Council president of Ashford Academy and granddaughter of its superintendent

debut.anime: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
debut.episodeTitle: The Day a New Demon was Born

milly-ashford.notes: Code Geass is an original anime, so there is no source chapter. Episode 1 rests on the Code Geass Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 1 does not name her. Her grandfather's name comes from the wiki; Wikipedia describes him as the school superintendent.
milly-ashford.abilities: President of the Ashford Academy student council, a cheerful, outgoing organiser of school festivals and events.

fate.detail: Milly survives the series and becomes a newscaster by the end of R2.

minori-kushieda.name: Minori Kushieda
minori-kushieda.role: Taiga Aisaka's best friend and Ryuuji Takasu's crush; captain of the girls' softball club
minori-kushieda.notes: The wiki gives chapter 1 of the first light novel; Wikipedia cites volume 1 for her introduction.
minori-kushieda.abilities: A hyperactive, endlessly cheerful girl who captains the girls' softball team and juggles several part-time jobs.

fate.detail: Nobody dies in Toradora!; Minori is alive at the end of the anime and light novels.

mitsuha-miyamizu.name: Mitsuha Miyamizu
mitsuha-miyamizu.role: Female protagonist; high school girl in rural Itomori who swaps bodies with Taki Tachibana
mitsuha-miyamizu.notes: Kimi no Na wa. (Your Name) is a 2016 original film, so episode is null and source is null; Makoto Shinkai's tie-in novel came out a month before the film. Later relationships left out to avoid spoilers.
mitsuha-miyamizu.abilities: A shrine maiden from rural Itomori who performs her family's traditions, such as braid-weaving and making kuchikamizake, and who starts swapping bodies with Taki.

fate.detail: In the original timeline she is killed when a fragment of the comet destroys Itomori in 2013, but Taki's warning gets the town evacuated; she survives and meets him years later in Tokyo.

miyoko-sahara.name: Miyoko Sahara
miyoko-sahara.role: Kind elementary school classmate who tried to befriend Shouko Nishimiya
miyoko-sahara.notes: There is no TV anime: Koe no Katachi (A Silent Voice) is a 2016 film, so episode is null. Chapter 1 rests on the Koe no Katachi Wiki only.
miyoko-sahara.abilities: A kind classmate who learns sign language to befriend Shouko, and later studies fashion design.

fate.detail: Miyoko is alive at the end of the film and manga.

nagisa-shiota.name: Nagisa Shiota
nagisa-shiota.role: Protagonist and narrator; student of Class 3-E at Kunugigaoka Junior High School
nagisa-shiota.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources; chapter 1 rests on the wiki only.
nagisa-shiota.abilities: Small and easily overlooked, he keeps detailed notes on Koro-sensei's weaknesses and shows a hidden, unsettling talent for assassination.

fate.detail: Nagisa survives the series and becomes a teacher in the epilogue.

nanachi.name: Nanachi
nanachi.role: Hollow (Narehate) living in the Abyss who helps Riko and Reg
nanachi.notes: Episode 10 is confirmed by both sources. Chapter 19 rests on the Made in Abyss Wiki only.
nanachi.abilities: A Narehate, transformed by the Abyss's curse yet clear-minded, with deep knowledge of the Abyss's creatures, plants and medicine, plus the ability to sense the curse's force field.

fate.detail: Nanachi is alive in the anime (two seasons and the Dawn of the Deep Soul film) and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

nidaime-raikage.name: A (Second Raikage)
nidaime-raikage.role: Second Raikage of Kumogakure; former bodyguard of the First Raikage
nidaime-raikage.notes: Episode 269 and chapter 527 debut rest on Narutopedia; the Wikipedia summary of episode 269 mentions the Second Raikage in a flashback about the Gold and Silver Brothers. His service as the First Raikage's bodyguard rests on Narutopedia only.

fate.detail: He died before the series began; he appears only as a spirit, summoned from the Pure Land with the other dead Kage by Hagoromo Otsutsuki to help undo the Infinite Tsukuyomi at the end of the Fourth Shinobi World War.

noelle-silva.name: Noelle Silva
noelle-silva.role: Royal of House Silva and Water Magic user in the Black Bulls squad
noelle-silva.notes: Chapter 4 ("The Black Bulls") is confirmed by both sources. Episode 4 rests on the Black Clover Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 4 does not name her.
noelle-silva.abilities: A royal of House Silva with enormous mana and water magic that she at first cannot control; her first controlled spell is the protective water sphere Sea Dragon's Nest.

fate.detail: Noelle is alive in the anime and in the manga's ongoing final arc (as of November 2026).

ochako-uraraka.name: Ochaco Uraraka
ochako-uraraka.role: Student in U.A. High School's Class 1-A; hero name Uravity
ochako-uraraka.notes: Chapter 3 ("Entrance Exam") is confirmed by both sources. Episode 3 rests on the My Hero Academia Wiki; the Wikipedia summary of episode 3 does not name her.
ochako-uraraka.abilities: Her Quirk, Zero Gravity, makes anything she touches with her fingertip pads weightless, though overusing it makes her nauseous.

fate.detail: Uraraka survives the final war against Toga and is alive at the series' end (manga final chapter 430, 2024).

phosphophyllite.name: Phosphophyllite
phosphophyllite.role: Protagonist; youngest of the Lustrous, assigned to compile a natural history encyclopedia
phosphophyllite.notes: Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms Phos is on the volume 1 cover.
phosphophyllite.abilities: The youngest and most fragile gem, too brittle to fight, who is given the task of compiling a natural history encyclopedia.

fate.detail: As an immortal gem Phos never simply dies: in the manga's ending (2024) Phos becomes a god-like being who prays the other gems and Lunarians away and, after the sun swallows the Earth, lives on only as a small gem shard; the anime (2017) ends long before this.

rei-kiriyama.name: Rei Kiriyama
rei-kiriyama.role: Protagonist; teenage professional shogi player who lives alone

debut.episodeTitle: Rei Kiriyama / The Town Along the River

rei-kiriyama.notes: Episode 1 has two segments; both titles are given. Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
rei-kiriyama.abilities: A 17-year-old professional shogi player, one of the few ever to turn pro in middle school.

fate.detail: Rei is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

riko-brzenska.name: Rico Brzenska
riko-brzenska.role: Team leader in the Garrison's elite squad

debut.episodeTitle: Whereabouts of His Left Arm: The Struggle for Trost, Part 5

riko-brzenska.notes: Episode 9 and chapter 10 ("Where's the Left Arm?", volume 3) debut rest on the Attack on Titan Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 11. Arc names follow the wiki's anime page.
riko-brzenska.abilities: An elite Garrison squad captain and skilled soldier with vertical manoeuvring equipment, known for her strict, by-the-book attitude.

fate.detail: Rico survives the Battle of Trost (where she leads Eren's escort) and is listed as alive at the end of the series.

rin-hoshizora.name: Rin Hoshizora
rin-hoshizora.role: Athletic first-year student at Otonokizaka Academy and member of the school idol group μ's
rin-hoshizora.notes: Love Live! is a multimedia project rather than an adaptation of a manga or light novel, so source is null. The episode 1 debut rests on the Love Live! Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 4.
rin-hoshizora.abilities: An energetic, athletic first-year and member of the idol group mu's, known for her cat-like 'nya' and boundless stamina.

fate.detail: Rin is alive at the end of the series and the 2015 movie; Love Live! has no character deaths.

rin-okumura.name: Rin Okumura
rin-okumura.role: Protagonist; son of Satan who trains as an exorcist at True Cross Academy

debut.episodeTitle: The Devil Resides in Human Souls

rin-okumura.notes: Arc names follow the Blue Exorcist Wiki (manga arcs). Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
rin-okumura.abilities: The son of Satan, whose demonic powers are sealed in the sword Kurikara; drawing it gives him blue flames, demonic strength and fast healing.

fate.detail: Rin is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

rin-tohsaka.name: Rin Tohsaka
rin-tohsaka.role: Master in the Fifth Holy Grail War who summons Archer; heir to the Tohsaka magecraft
rin-tohsaka.notes: Fate/stay night is a visual novel, so source is null. Episode 0 ("Prologue") opens the Unlimited Blade Works TV series from her point of view. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
rin-tohsaka.abilities: A gifted mage of the Tohsaka family and Archer's Master, who stores mana in jewels for gem magecraft and fires Gandr curse shots.

fate.detail: Rin survives the Fifth Holy Grail War in Unlimited Blade Works and leaves for the Clock Tower in London with Shirou.

robin-nico.name: Nico Robin
robin-nico.role: Archaeologist of the Straw Hat Pirates; formerly Miss All Sunday of Baroque Works

debut.episodeTitle: Deliver Princess Vivi! The Luffy Pirates Set Sail!

robin-nico.notes: Arcs listed are pre-timeskip arcs from the wiki's history page; she also takes part in later Straw Hat arcs.
robin-nico.abilities: An archaeologist who can read the ancient Poneglyphs; her Hana Hana no Mi Devil Fruit lets her sprout copies of her body parts, such as arms, on any surface.

fate.detail: Robin is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026); she nearly dies at Enies Lobby but is rescued by the Straw Hats.

sanji.name: Sanji
sanji.role: Cook of the Straw Hat Pirates; former sous-chef of the Baratie

debut.episodeTitle: Famous Cook! Sanji of the Sea Restaurant!

sanji.notes: Arcs listed are pre-timeskip arcs from the wiki's history page; he also takes part in later Straw Hat arcs. Birth family left out to avoid spoilers.
sanji.abilities: The Straw Hats' cook, who fights only with powerful kicks (Black Leg Style) to keep his hands safe for cooking.

fate.detail: Sanji is alive in the anime and in the ongoing manga (as of November 2026).

satoru-fujinuma.name: Satoru Fujinuma
satoru-fujinuma.role: Protagonist; struggling manga artist with a time-travel ability called Revival
satoru-fujinuma.notes: Arc names follow the Boku Dake ga Inai Machi Wiki.
satoru-fujinuma.abilities: A struggling manga artist with "Revival", an involuntary ability that sends him back a few minutes in time to prevent an imminent tragedy.

fate.detail: Satoru survives: the killer throws him into a river and he spends years in a coma, but he wakes up, helps catch the culprit and finally succeeds as a manga artist (anime and manga endings differ in details).

satoshi-mashiba.name: Satoshi Mashiba
satoshi-mashiba.role: High school boy who joins Shoya Ishida's group of friends
satoshi-mashiba.notes: There is no TV anime: Koe no Katachi (A Silent Voice) is a 2016 film, so episode is null. Chapter 24 rests on the Koe no Katachi Wiki only.

fate.detail: Mashiba is alive at the end of both the manga and the 2016 film.

shidou-itsuka.name: Shido Itsuka
shidou-itsuka.role: Protagonist; high school student recruited by Ratatoskr to seal the powers of Spirits
shidou-itsuka.notes: Light novel debut is volume 1. Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
shidou-itsuka.abilities: An ordinary high-schooler with a mysterious power to seal a Spirit's powers by making her fall in love with him and kissing her, plus rapid regeneration from wounds.

fate.detail: Shido survives to the end of the Date A Live light novels (concluded 2020) and is alive in the anime.

shinji-ikari.name: Shinji Ikari
shinji-ikari.notes: Neon Genesis Evangelion is an original anime, so source is null; the Yoshiyuki Sadamoto manga, which began in 1994, runs alongside it and also opens with "Angel Attack". Other relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
shinji-ikari.abilities: A 14-year-old who, despite no training, shows a remarkably high synch ratio piloting Evangelion Unit-01 against the Angels.

fate.detail: Shinji survives both endings: The End of Evangelion leaves him alive with Asuka after Third Impact, and Evangelion: 3.0+1.0 (2021) ends with him alive as an adult.

shizuka-marikawa.name: Shizuka Marikawa
shizuka-marikawa.role: School nurse at Fujimi High School who escapes with the student survivors
shizuka-marikawa.notes: Episode 1 rests on the Highschool of the Dead Wiki; Wikipedia episode summaries first name her in episode 2. Manga chapter not confirmed.
shizuka-marikawa.abilities: Fujimi High's ditzy school nurse, whose medical knowledge makes her the group's doctor; she also drives them out of the school.

fate.detail: Shizuka is alive at the end of the anime and of the manga, which was left unfinished after writer Daisuke Satō died in 2017.

shouko-nishimiya.name: Shouko Nishimiya
shouko-nishimiya.role: Co-lead; deaf girl who was bullied by Shoya Ishida in elementary school
shouko-nishimiya.notes: There is no TV anime: Koe no Katachi (A Silent Voice) is a 2016 film, so episode is null. Chapter 1 per the wiki; Wikipedia confirms she is on the volume 1 cover.
shouko-nishimiya.abilities: A deaf girl who communicates through a notebook and sign language, and who stays kind even toward people who hurt her.

fate.detail: Shoko attempts suicide by jumping from her balcony, but Shoya saves her (manga and 2016 film); she survives the series.

shura-kirigakure.name: Shura Kirigakure
shura-kirigakure.role: Upper First Class Exorcist of the True Cross Order who trained under Shiro Fujimoto
shura-kirigakure.notes: She first appears disguised as the student "Yamada" (episode 3, chapter 2 per the Blue Exorcist Wiki only); Wikipedia confirms her reveal as herself in episode 12. Arc names follow the wiki. Relatives left out to avoid spoilers.
shura-kirigakure.abilities: An Upper First Class Exorcist and Vatican inspector, a Meister-level Knight (swordswoman) and Doctor who draws a demon sword from a seal on her body and trains Rin.

fate.detail: Shura is alive in the anime and the ongoing manga (as of November 2026); the Beyond the Snow arc deals with the family curse that dooms her at age 30.

sora-2.name: Sora
sora-2.role: Co-protagonist; half of the undefeated gamer duo Blank
sora-2.notes: The light novel debut is volume 1; Wikipedia confirms he is on the volume 1 cover. Later family members left out to avoid spoilers.
sora-2.abilities: Half of the undefeated gamer duo 'Blank' with his sister Shiro; he excels at reading people, bluffing and long-term strategy.

fate.detail: Sora is alive in the anime, the 2017 film and the ongoing light novels.

stephanie-dora.name: Stephanie Dola
stephanie-dora.role: Granddaughter of the previous king of Elkia who becomes the aide of Sora and Shiro
stephanie-dora.notes: Episode 1 is confirmed by both sources. Light novel volume 1 and her grandfather's name rest on the No Game No Life Wiki; Wikipedia mentions the grandfather without naming him.
stephanie-dora.abilities: The granddaughter of Elkia's late king, a noble with good schooling but poor luck at games, who handles the kingdom's administration.

fate.detail: Steph is alive in the anime and the ongoing light novels.

suzaku-kururugi.name: Suzaku Kururugi
suzaku-kururugi.role: Japanese-born soldier in the Britannian Army who pilots the Lancelot; Lelouch's childhood friend

debut.anime: Code Geass: Lelouch of the Rebellion
